verdict.rationale: Deepgram's trust docs say requests join the Model Improvement Program by default, and users can opt out per request with mip_opt_out=true, after which requests are not retained. This is a first-party control against model-training use. Its extent is unproven: it is opt-out rather than opt-in, it is set per request, and the evidence never confirms it applies to the Voice Agent WebSocket endpoint. Missing for 10: explicit confirmation that mip_opt_out works on the Voice Agent API, an account-level or default opt-out, explicit no-training terms for third-party LLM providers in the agent pipeline, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can prevent my data from being used to train AI models

citations.quote: Opt out per request with mip_opt_out=true. Opted-out requests are not retained
Requests participate in the Model Improvement Program (MIP) by default, and Deepgram retains them
